source.publication: Publication 120 Retirement Income (December 2025), with the 2025 IL-1040 Instructions and Form IL-1040
source.section: Pub 120 PDF page 2, Social Security bullet ('federally taxed portion (not the gross amount)'); Form IL-1040 PDF page 1, Lines 1-19; Instructions PDF page 8, Lines 10-12; rate Instructions PDF page 1; Line 10a chart and Income Exceptions, Instructions PDF page 8; Line 10b, Instructions PDF page 8 and Form IL-1040 PDF page 1

worked: Federal AGI = taxable Social Security (of 30,000.00 gross) 25,500.00 + interest 53,850.00 = 79,350.00. Federal taxable income = 79,350.00 - standard deduction 15,750.00 - additional amount for 1 person(s) 65 or older 2,000.00 = 61,600.00 (federal senior deduction ignored; federal figures are given, not tested; Illinois starts from federal AGI). Form IL-1040 Line 1 federal AGI 79,350.00. Line 2 federally tax-exempt interest 0.00. Line 3 other additions 0.00. Line 4 = 79,350.00. Line 5 federally taxed Social Security 25,500.00 = 25,500.00. Lines 6 and 7 0.00. Line 8 = 25,500.00. Line 9 base income = 79,350.00 - 25,500.00 = 53,850.00. Income Exceptions: federal AGI 79,350.00 is not greater than 250,000.00, so the allowance stands. Line 10a 2,850.00. Line 10b 1,000.00 (1 box(es) x 1,000.00). Lines 10c and 10d 0.00. Line 10 = 3,850.00. Line 11 net income = 53,850.00 - 3,850.00 = 50,000.00. Line 12 tax = 50,000.00 x 4.95% = 2,475.0000. Lines 13-18 0.00 (no credits in the projection). Line 19 state income tax = 2,475.00. Only the 25,500.00 inside federal AGI comes off on Line 5, not the 30,000.00 gross.
